summary:
This application is the backend for an online shop that lets shoppers browse a product catalog, register an account, place orders, and have those orders paid for automatically, while inventory is reserved and replenished behind the scenes. A shopper looks at what's for sale, creates an account, submits an order for one or more products, and the system takes over from there: it prices the order from the live catalog, sets aside the needed stock, and charges the shopper through a payment gateway.

The primary users are shoppers — browsing products, registering, placing orders, and reviewing their own order history — identified on each authenticated request via a bearer-style user context rather than a visible login flow. A store-operations/merchant role maintains the catalog by adding new products. Behind the scenes, placing an order fires an order-placed event that inventory and payment react to independently: inventory reserves stock for the ordered lines, and payment charges the order total through a gateway abstraction, with stock levels also topped up automatically by a background restock job so popular items don't stay unavailable.

Structurally, the business is organized around five capabilities coordinating through one shared event bus and one underlying data store — a product catalog, customer accounts, order placement/history, inventory reservation and restocking, and payment charging. It reads as a single-store retail operation (one catalog, one set of customers, one order pipeline) rather than a multi-vendor marketplace.

useCases.title: Place an order
useCases.description: A shopper buys one or more products in a single order; the order is priced from the live catalog, triggers a stock reservation, and is charged through payment.
steps: Shopper submits a PlaceOrderRequest with the desired product line items via POST to the orders endpoint
Order service looks up each product's current price from the catalog (PriceOf)
Order and its order lines are recorded and an order-placed event is published on the shared bus
Inventory's order-placed handler reserves stock for each ordered line
Payment service charges the shopper for the order total via the gateway
useCases.evidence: orders.PlaceOrder; PlaceOrderRequest/LineItem in orders/model.go; bus.Publish/Subscribe; catalog.PriceOf; inventory.OnOrderPlaced

useCases.title: Pay for an order
useCases.description: The shopper's order total is automatically charged through a payment gateway as part of placing the order, completing the purchase.
steps: Order placement triggers a charge request for the order total
Payment service forwards the charge to the payment gateway (Gateway.Charge)
Payment outcome is recorded as a Payment tied to the order

useCases.title: Have stock reserved automatically when an order is placed
useCases.description: When a shopper places an order, the requested quantities are automatically set aside from inventory so the order can be fulfilled without being oversold.
steps: Inventory subscribes to order-placed events on the shared bus
When an order is placed, inventory's OnOrderPlaced handler runs
Inventory reserves the ordered quantity of each product (Reserve) against the StockItem records

useCases.title: Browse available products
useCases.description: A shopper views the current product catalog with pricing before deciding what to buy.
steps: Shopper requests the product listing via GET on the products endpoint
Catalog service returns the available products (List) with current prices and categories

useCases.title: View my order history
useCases.description: An authenticated customer reviews the orders they've previously placed.
steps: Customer requests their order history via the 'my orders' endpoint
Auth middleware resolves the requesting customer's identity from the request context (UserID)
Order service returns all orders tied to that customer (ForCustomer)
useCases.evidence: orders.ForCustomer; myOrders handler; AuthMiddleware/UserID in platform/auth.go

useCases.title: Register a customer account
useCases.description: A new shopper creates an account so they can place orders and be identified on future requests.
steps: Shopper submits registration details via POST on the customers endpoint
Customer service creates and stores the new account (Register)

useCases.title: Look up a customer's account details
useCases.description: An account holder retrieves their stored account details by ID.
steps: Account holder requests account details via GET on the customer endpoint by ID
Customer service returns the account record (Get)

useCases.title: Add a new product to the catalog
useCases.description: A store operator adds a new product listing with a price and category to the catalog for shoppers to buy.
steps: Merchant submits new product details (including price and category) via POST on the products endpoint
Catalog service creates and stores the new product record (Create)

useCases.title: Have out-of-stock items automatically replenished
useCases.description: The store keeps products available by automatically replenishing stock on a recurring schedule, without manual reordering.
steps: A background restock job starts and runs on a recurring interval (StartRestockJob)
Each run replenishes StockItem quantities that have fallen low (Restock)
